subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Service quality and service failures across the airline journey (crew, ground, food, complaint handling), treated as the aspect most worth analyzing

per_column.name: cabin_crew_demeanor
per_column.rationale: A concrete facet of in-flight service quality (attitude/behaviour of crew), directly central to a service-experience focus.

per_column.name: food_quality_signal
per_column.rationale: Captures the catering/meal facet of the service experience, with meaningful failure modes (special_meal_failure, ran_out_of_choice).

per_column.name: ground_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Extends the service focus to the pre/post-flight touchpoints (check-in, gate), a distinct but coherent facet.

per_column.name: complaint_resolution_outcome
per_column.rationale: Service-recovery dimension: how well failures were handled. Complements the failure facets and is highly on-focus.

per_column.name: service_failure_severity
per_column.rationale: An aggregate severity gradient over the service experience; ties the individual facets into an overall failure-intensity axis.

per_column.name: cabin_class_product_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Slightly more product/value-oriented than pure service, but still frames delivered experience vs. expectation, so it stays within the same coherent concept (least central of the set).

per_column.name: service_consistency_signal
per_column.rationale: A temporal-consistency facet of service quality; on-focus, though its data-inferability from a single review is somewhat strained.

judge.rationale: The query names no focus, so the system had to propose one. Six of seven columns converge tightly on a single, data-inferable concept — service quality/service failure across the journey (crew demeanor, ground service, food, complaint resolution, overall severity, consistency), with only cabin_class_product_mismatch drifting slightly toward product/value. This is clearly ONE coherent focus rather than a scattered grab-bag, so coherence is high. The structure is well differentiated: multiple distinct service facets (crew, ground, food, recovery) plus an aggregating severity axis and a temporal-consistency signal, at a useful categorical granularity with informative failure modes — not a single restatement nor undifferentiated noise; the one small weakness is that service_failure_severity partly overlaps as a roll-up of the facets and consistency is hard to infer per-review, so structure is strong but not perfect. The implied focus (service failures and their resolution) is exactly the kind of thing an airline analyst can act on — target crew training, ground operations, catering, and complaint handling — so actionability is high. Not marked as failing on any dimension because the set genuinely realises a coherent, structured, actionable inferred focus rather than generic length/sentiment filler.
